column9: Chapter 1, question on supply chains, pp. 72-73: "Similarly, Japan faces rising costs in adopting near-zero emissions production, primarily as a result of high energy costs due to geographical constraints. Its competitive advantage, however, lies in value-added industries further down the supply chain. The Middle East, by contrast, benefits from abundant renewable energy resources, making low-emissions ammonia imports from this region a more cost-effective option for Japan; urea cost premiums would fall from approximately 80% to 55%."
